html:
A great earthquake that struck the northern Tian Shan on 3 January 1911, centred in the Chon-Kemin valley of today's Kyrgyzstan, east of Bishkek. With a magnitude of about 8, it is one of the strongest earthquakes known in Central Asia.

It tore open the ground along about 200 km of the valleys of the Chon-Kemin, Chilik and Chon-Aksu. In the Russian town of Verny, now Almaty, it destroyed almost all of the brick buildings, and about 450 people were killed in the region. The wooden Ascension Cathedral in Verny survived. The town was rebuilt with lower, sturdier buildings.

The Tian Shan rises because India keeps pushing north into Asia, and the region still stores strain for future quakes. A few weeks later the Sarez earthquake in the Pamirs dammed a whole valley. Other quakes of the region on this chart include the Ashgabat earthquake of 1948 and the Tashkent earthquake of 1966.
